summary: Admission accepts a transport-confirmed chunk whose text is any substring, but the durable history validator (models.py:1520) requires it to equal the whole generated segment text, so a multi-chunk segment is admitted and then refused at the store.
failure_scenario: A user-response segment 'First sentence. Second sentence.' is synthesized as two SpeechChunks (streaming.py:1904-1911 locates each chunk by text.find with a cursor, so sub-segment chunks are an intended path); try_admit_transport_confirmed_full (admission.py:3329-3407) passes only chunk_ordinal/lineage checks in _turn_event_is_valid_locked and returns ADMITTED with the chunk text from ledger.confirmed_text (the per-chunk text). When the writer appends, sqlite_spool.py:2149 runs validate_event_sequence, which raises 'confirmed text does not match its segment', and the spool returns CONFLICT_TAINTED/LINEAGE_INVALID: the confirmation is not stored and the session is tainted, so the evidence for that turn is lost although admission reported success.
evidence: Isolated stdlib repro (scratchpad/repro.py, PYTHONPATH=src, no pytest available): validate_event_sequence accepts a history with one confirmation whose text equals the segment (control) and raises _EvidenceValueError('confirmed text does not match its segment') for two chunk confirmations ['First sentence.','Second sentence.'] of the same segment. Static reads: admission.py _turn_event_is_valid_locked (confirmation branch checks only turn id, readiness, chunk ordinal), try_admit_transport_confirmed_full, streaming.py 1677-1686 and 1904-1936, delivery.py 275-289 (confirmed_text returns chunk.text), sqlite_spool.py 2149-2154. Not run end to end: no real chunker or spool exercised, so whether a given provider yields multiple chunks per segment in production is unproven; the spec/validator versus admission mismatch is proven.

summary: Prior claim speech/delivery.py:231 (begin_turn discards delivery-context-recorded flag on every queue()): confirmed by static read (queue calls begin_turn(chunk.turn_id) at line 218 and begin_turn does _delivery_context_recorded_turns.discard unconditionally at line 227). File is outside my slice and I did not reproduce the effect on assistant_delivery_context_recorded in settle_terminal; unresolved witness: a two-chunk turn run through the real ledger and streaming settle path.

Prior claims for other files (api.py, plugin.py, bridge.py, preview_cutover.py, evidence_presentation.py, sqlite_spool.py, review.py, worker.py, web/*, scripts/*, workflows) are outside assigned files and not examined; no disposition given.

lifecycle.py: final-input authority is single-use (consumed under the lock on route/retire), cleared on close_binding, seal, and rollover commit; rollover prepare/commit/abort checks predecessor identity by equality and blocks activate/close/seal while prepared; conversation_authority_is_current compares owner generation and the full binding lineage including logical session, so post-rollover bearers are stale. No defect found.

runtime.py EvidenceWriterDispatcherV1: every payload type has a matching fault completion for transport exceptions and for wrong-type or disallowed dispositions, releasing charges once; ordered-item success is derived from an exact allowed-set membership. BoundedEvidenceWriterQueueV1 serves revoke, then ordered FIFO, then drain, and rejects puts after consumer stop. No defect found on static read.

admission.py try_rollover / capacity rollover claim / enqueue_prepared_rollover / reject / abort: charge, ordinal rollback and phase restore are symmetric on each failure branch (queue put failure, ordinal mismatch, invalid composition); active leases and replayable turns block rollover. No defect found. Note settle_* methods convert caller count errors (e.g. snapshot count contradictions, empty cause set) into a sticky SQLITE_FAULT; this is fail-closed, not reported as a defect.

models.py validate_event_sequence: contiguous sequence, single opening records, utterance single-consumption, no events after settlement, snapshot counts equal preceding records, settlement counts equal snapshot, replay lineage and retry rules are enforced by equality; terminal pair table and cause precedence are consistent. Apart from the finding above, no defect found.

Limitations: pytest, ruff and mypy are not installed in this environment, so the project test suite was not run; evidence is static reading plus one stdlib repro against models.py. Tests in the assigned test files were not individually audited for enshrined wrong behavior beyond grepping for multi-chunk confirmation coverage (none found).
